title: Reason Code 65 — denied by the account's Network Access Permission
plain_english: Everything else was fine — the user's own AD account says no. The 'Network Access Permission' setting on the account's Dial-in tab is set to 'Deny access', and that overrides your NPS policies. This is a per-account setting, so it typically hits one user while everyone else connects normally.

causes.cause: The account's Dial-in tab is explicitly set to 'Deny access' (sometimes by an old script, migration, or a well-meaning colleague).
causes.next_check: In ADUC, open the user → Dial-in tab → set Network Access Permission to 'Control access through NPS Network Policy'.

causes.cause: Bulk-set msNPAllowDialin attribute from a legacy RAS era still lingering on many accounts.
causes.next_check: Query AD for accounts with msNPAllowDialin=FALSE to see whether this is one user or hundreds.

causes.cause: You want NPS policies to be authoritative but the policy still honours per-account settings.
causes.next_check: In the matched network policy's properties, enable 'Ignore user account dial-in properties' so the policy decides, not the account flag.
